text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Monday its oil and condensate production was up two percent in the 11 months to April compared with a year earlier but gas production, including LNG, was down five percent.
Oil and condensate production for the 11 months to April 30 totalled 63.375 million barrels, including 6.015 million barrels in April, which was up three percent on a year earlier.
Gas production totalled 19 billion cubic feet in the month of April, down 10 percent from a year earlier, to bring year to date production to 225.7 million tonnes.

BHP said total oil and condensate production for April was higher compared with the same month a year earlier and year to date, mainly due to production associated with the commencement of the Liverpool Bay project in the United Kingdom.
Bass Strait output was higher in April due to contributions from West Tuna, Bream B and the Cobia infill drilling programme.
The Griffin Venture production vessel was disconnected from the riser on April 26 and entered Fremantle in early May for a previously announced four to six week remediation and maintenance programme.
BHP said production from the Griffin Venture was also affected by the temporary cessation of production from three wells (Scindian 1 and 2 and Griffin 5) associated with flow-line difficulties.

BHP said total gas production declined in April compared with a year earlier and on a year to date basis due to lower domestic production and demand, and the lower contribution from the Americas, associated with asset divestments.
This was offset to some extent by increased gas sales from both Liverpool Bay and the Bruce and Ravenspurn North fields in the North Sea.
